hull.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit for Hull
s1loc: Hull leans on a deep food-aid network. FareShare Hull and Humber, run from the Goodwin Development Trust, redistributes surplus food and runs a membership Community Pantry, while Hull Foodbank has fed people in crisis since 2011 as part of the Trussell network. Hull CVS, founded in 1981, backs volunteer and community groups across the city, including small grants for projects on the Bransholme estate, and Dove House Hospice cares for families across Hull and the East Riding.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying behind them, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Orchard Park, Bransholme, Hessle Road and the city centre. Faith groups, mutual-aid teams and community fridges all add to the mix. We can clothe the national charity with its trade account and the one-room foodbank ordering direct online, no minimum, with equal care.

derby.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit for Derby
s1loc: Derby has a long-standing food-aid backbone. Derby City Mission on Normanton Road runs the city foodbank alongside debt and advice clinics, and most parcels lean on donated stock plus surplus from FareShare. Community Action Derby supports volunteer and community groups across the city and runs Warm Welcome Hubs, while Treetops Hospice, based at Risley, cares for adults with life-limiting conditions across central and southern Derbyshire. Rural Action Derbyshire helps seed community shops and pantries in the harder-pressed areas.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities carry shops and central buying, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects scrape by on a shoestring across Normanton, Sinfin, Allenton and Chaddesden. Faith groups, mutual-aid teams and affordable-food schemes round out the picture. Derby's emergency-food map is dense and locally run. Derby City Mission operates its long-running foodbank from Normanton Road and coordinates parcels across the city, while the Padley Group runs the Padley@YMCA Derbyshire community pantry on Parcel Terrace alongside its homelessness and complex-needs work. Doorways Derby Foodbank sits on Osmaston Park Road in Allenton, and church and centre-based provision reaches out through Alvaston Churches Together and Sinfin Community Centre. FareShare Midlands feeds surplus into many of these projects, and Community Action Derby threads the voluntary sector together, running Warm Welcome Hubs at sites such as Sinfin Community Centre and St Martin's in Allenton. Treetops Hospice Care, based at Risley near the city, draws fundraising and volunteer effort from across Derby and south Derbyshire. From Normanton and Sinfin to Alvaston and Allenton, the picture is small Christian missions, neighbourhood pantries and big redistribution networks all leaning on local volunteers who give time sorting, packing and driving week after week. Foundation Derbyshire channels grants to grassroots groups across the city and county, supporting volunteer-run pantries, community centres and charity shops the length of Derby.

Mountbatten Hampshire, the local hospice, runs care and a chain of charity shops serving Southampton, Eastleigh and the wider county.

s1loc: Stoke-on-Trent has a tight community sector. Stoke-on-Trent Foodbank has helped local people since 2012 as part of the Trussell network, with collection points across the six towns, and VAST is the city's voluntary-sector support body that backs the StokeOnTrentTogether food work. FareShare Midlands feeds surplus stock to organisations across the West Midlands, and the city runs a string of community pantries that help residents cut weekly food bills.

wolverhampton.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit for Wolverhampton
s1loc: Wolverhampton has a strong front line of help. The Good Shepherd on Waterloo Road serves hot meals and hands out family food bags, while FoodCycle Wolverhampton cooks free community meals from surplus food. Wolverhampton Voluntary and Community Action, formerly WVSC, supports local charities, community groups and social enterprises, and Compton Care provides hospice care across the city and beyond. FareShare Midlands keeps surplus food flowing to organisations right across the West Midlands.

Swansea Council for Voluntary Service, the SCVS, is the umbrella body backing volunteers and community groups across the city, and Ty Olwen at Morriston Hospital provides specialist palliative and hospice care.

milton keynes.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit for Milton Keynes
s1loc: Milton Keynes has a busy food-aid network. MK Food Bank offers short-term crisis support to families and individuals across the city, and FareShare South Midlands, based in Bletchley and run with the charity SOFEA, has redistributed surplus food to charities and community groups since 2019. The MK Community Fridge is open to all with no criteria for sharing food, and Willen Hospice provides specialist palliative care for people across Milton Keynes and the surrounding area.

Milton Keynes has a fast-growing voluntary sector for a new city. MK Food Bank, in the Trussell network, runs distribution centres across the city from its Kiln Farm base, while Milton Keynes Community Foundation funds hundreds of grassroots groups and MK SNAP supports adults with learning disabilities. Willen Hospice raises funds through a chain of charity shops, and community projects in Bletchley, Wolverton and Stony Stratford lean on volunteers for collections, pantries and events.
